My family has worked this land for decades and I know what grows here. Quzhou is flat, fertile ground — wheat and maize country. That's what I'll grow. I have 12 mu total. I'll put 10 mu into the wheat-maize rotation like every year, and keep 2 mu near the house for garlic, which I plant in autumn and sell at the township market in spring to bring in some extra cash before wheat harvest.

For winter wheat, I'll sow in mid-October. I'll use 矮抗58 — I've used it for years, it handles the rust well and gives me reliable yield. I'll plow and rotary-till first, apply compound base fertilizer at sowing, then top-dress with urea in early spring at greening. I irrigate three times: the winter irrigation before the ground freezes, jointing stage in April, and once at grain fill. My brother says two waterings is enough but I've seen dry Mays before and I won't risk my yield. I'll spray herbicide in autumn after emergence, fungicide in spring when the flag leaf appears, and aphid control at heading — three applications total.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll plant maize directly into the stubble — no tillage, just use the cooperative's planter. Hybrid seed, same as everyone here. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea at the big bell stage. Summer usually brings rain so I'll only irrigate at planting if the soil is dry. Two pesticide applications: herbicide right after planting, and one insecticide pass if I see corn borer pressure.

For the 2 mu of garlic I'll plow in early October before planting, since it needs loose soil. I use traditional cloves saved from last year's crop. Garlic needs potassium — I apply more than I do for grain crops. I'll irrigate four times through winter and spring. Price has been decent the last two years so I'll keep this plot.
